items.title: Define the v2 record union with exhaustive per-operation field sets and always-present nullable chain fields
items.context: packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/record-v2.ts declares the proofstory.red_evidence.v2 union with the exhaustive per-operation field sets of §1.10 (lines 591-721); the §0.4 chain fields seq/priorRecordDigest/supersedes are ALWAYS present and carry JSON null at seq==1; recordDigest = W2a CANON over the record with recordDigest omitted; specDigest per §1.10.

happy.desc: Construct a red-assert v2 record with all §1.10 fields; verify recordDigest = CANON(record minus recordDigest field) and specDigest = CANON({acceptanceTargetRef, greenRelation:{targetRef, relation}}); WHY: confirms digest derivation matches spec exactly

Construct a quarantine v2 record; verify it carries ONLY the quarantine/recover field set (chain fields, storyId, acceptanceTargetRef, recoversRecordId, referencedRecordDigest, linkKind=quarantines, reason, approvedBy, operationKey, createdAt, recordDigest) and OMITS assertion/policySnapshot/runReceipt/baselineHeadHash/specDigest; WHY: §0.4 omission rules — field not listed is OMITTED not null

Verify chain fields seq/priorRecordDigest/supersedes are ALWAYS present on every v2 record type; at seq==1 both priorRecordDigest and supersedes carry JSON null (not omitted, not empty string); WHY: §0.4 nullability rule for chain-founding records

edge.desc: Construct a green-confirm record; verify it has confirmsRecordId/confirmsRecordDigest/confirmsAssertionDigest but NO assertion/policySnapshot of its own; redBaselineHeadHash/redBaselineMaterialHash present; WHY: green-confirm reuses the governing red-assert assertion via confirmsAssertionDigest

Construct a recover record; verify its field set is identical to quarantine (same control-record shape) except linkKind=recovers; verify no specDigest, no greenRelation; WHY: quarantine/recover are chain-control records with the same idempotency preimage shape

adversarial.desc: Attempt to include a field that belongs to a different operation (e.g. runReceipt on a quarantine record, or trigger on a recover) — type system or runtime validator rejects; WHY: exhaustive per-operation field sets are a closed contract, extra fields = spec violation

Set priorRecordDigest to empty string (not null) at seq==1; recompute recordDigest — verify it differs from the canonical null form; WHY: empty-string-vs-null divergence would fork digests across hosts

items.title: Widen RedEvidenceData to a mixed v1 and v2 records array without changing the stored file layout
items.context: packages/main/src/core/types.ts:2700 RedEvidenceData.records[] is widened to hold mixed v1 and v2 records in one array with the same on-disk file layout (schemaVersion-discriminated); no migration of existing v1 stores.

happy.desc: Read a store with v1-only records; round-trip write and re-read; all v1 records retain schemaVersion proofstory.red_evidence.v1 and their original shape; WHY: no migration means v1 stores are untouched
Read a store with mixed v1 + v2 records; both schemaVersion discriminators parse correctly; v1 records are not widened or rewritten; WHY: the mixed array is the core data model change

edge.desc: Empty records array parses and round-trips as an empty array; WHY: boundary condition for stores with no evidence yet
A store containing only v2 records (zero v1) parses correctly; WHY: new stories may never have v1 records

adversarial.desc: A record with an unknown schemaVersion (e.g. proofstory.red_evidence.v3) is rejected at parse/load time with a diagnostic, not silently accepted into the array; WHY: forward-compatibility must fail closed

items.title: Make redEvidenceRecordSatisfied skip every non-v1 record and prove all three gate verdicts are unchanged
items.context: In the SAME commit as the widening: guard redEvidenceRecordSatisfied (packages/main/src/core/proofstory.ts:931) so its record.observedFailure.trim() at :932 (reached via .some() at :947 and missingRedEvidence at :1196) is only applied to v1 records — a v2 record must not crash the LIVE enforce gate (devGateMode/reviewGateMode/doneGateMode all enforce in lattice.config.json). Prove the diagnostic output is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the pre-change run on a v1-only store (RED signal A).

happy.desc: RED signal A baseline: on a v1-only store, capture the FULL diagnostic output of redEvidenceRecordSatisfied/missingRedEvidence BEFORE the change; after the change, capture the same output on the SAME v1-only store; outputs are BYTE-IDENTICAL (diff returns 0); WHY: the v1-skip guard must be transparent to all v1 paths — devGateMode/reviewGateMode/doneGateMode all enforce

On a mixed v1+v2 store where the v1 record satisfies the gate: proofstory_gate_check does NOT throw; v2 records are silently skipped; the v1 verdict is correct; WHY: v2 records must be invisible to the v1 gate predicate

edge.desc: A store with ONLY v2 records (no v1): missingRedEvidence fires (no v1 record satisfies the predicate); the diagnostic names the target as missing; WHY: v2-only stores have no satisfying v1 record and must report missing, not crash
A v1 record with empty-string observedFailure: gate still rejects (trim() yields empty → unsatisfied); WHY: the guard change must not alter any v1 evaluation path

adversarial.desc: RED signal A attack: write a v2 quarantine record (no observedFailure field) into a real story red-evidence.json; run the real proofstory_gate_check → must NOT throw TypeError at record.observedFailure.trim(); WHY: this is the exact live crash path (proofstory.ts:932 via .some() at :947 from missingRedEvidence at :1196) that throws today and must be fixed

Inject a record with schemaVersion proofstory.red_evidence.v2 but WITH an observedFailure field present (a malformed hybrid): the version discriminator governs the skip, not field presence; the record is still skipped by the v1 predicate; WHY: defense-in-depth against malformed records

items.title: Resolve the chain head by both uniqueness conjuncts and enforce the three chain-integrity checks
items.context: packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/chain.ts partitions records by (storyId, acceptanceTargetRef); head resolution implements BOTH §3.2 (lines 957-964) conjuncts; the three §3.3 (965-992) integrity checks run with FORK rejection as an INDEPENDENT store-corruption/concurrency detector whose reason id is DISTINCT from the prior-digest (check 2) rejection.

items.title: Implement the closed transition table with transitive cycle-safe effective-head resolution
items.context: The §3.3 closed transition table governs legal quarantine/recover transitions with governing-red-assert derivation; effective-head resolution walks transitively through chained recover records and is cycle-safe (a self-referential or looping recover chain TERMINATES instead of recursing forever).

items.title: Derive the three operation-key preimages and the deterministic record id from the digest body
items.context: packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/operation-key.ts derives the three §3.4 (1000-1050) operation-key preimages and normalizedReason, and the deterministic record id `<OP>-first12hex(operationKey)-<seq>`; first12hex reuses the W2a helper over the 64-hex body excluding the sha256: prefix.

items.title: Order the append pipeline so the dedupe search precedes head resolution and any run
items.context: packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/append.ts runs the mandated §3.5 ORDER: derive key → dedupe search → replay short-circuit (a replay deriving the same operationKey returns the EXISTING record, records.length UNCHANGED, no second run) → resolve head → transition legality → integrity checks → append; a stored record failing its own key/id recomputation raises a tagged CONFLICT with nothing written.

items.title: Scope the dedupe search so a quarantined record cannot swallow the deliberate replacement append
items.context: The §3.5 dedupe search is scoped (§3.6 lines 1067-1076) so a prior quarantine record cannot silently swallow a deliberate replacement append for the same target — the deliberate replacement is a genuine new record, not a dedupe hit.

items.title: Serialize every chain append under one mkdir claim covering read-head, dedupe, validate and write
items.context: All four chain appends are serialized under ONE atomic mkdir claim covering read-head through write, modeled on the executable acquireMkdirLock pattern at packages/main/src/handlers/transition-orchestrator.ts:812-836 (acquire :819, release :859) via packages/main/src/core/mkdir-lock.ts:253 — NOT the §4.1 line-1171 citation (an explanatory comment). Two racing red_evidence_quarantine processes yield exactly one record + a unique head; the loser reports a held-claim abort (RED signal B).

items.title: Land red_evidence_quarantine and red_evidence_recover with derived approvedBy and the binding freeze rule
items.context: packages/main/src/handlers/red-evidence.ts adds red_evidence_quarantine and red_evidence_recover (reusing the W2b 13-point wiring recipe: registry/command-catalog/command-policy/config/process-fact-levels/process-fact-registry/types union/permittedMutations/owner-lease), with the §4.1 (1122-1171) reference-validation state machine, DERIVED approvedBy = <actor>@<sessionId> (never a caller argument), recover-of-a-recover + quarantine-of-non-head rejected; and lands the §1.1.3 binding-freeze rule inside red_evidence_binding_set now that chain-head semantics exist (a binding is frozen once a run record exists on an unquarantined chain).

items.title: Register red-evidence-chain-smoke in lattice.config.json validate.commands and run the full suite
items.context: packages/main/src/tasks/red-evidence-chain-smoke.ts covers the v2 union, the enforce-gate byte-identical guard, the chain integrity checks + transition table, the operation-key/dedupe/replay ordering, the mkdir-claim concurrency race, the full rejection matrix, and quarantine/recover + binding-freeze; register it in lattice.config.json validate.commands and update the four verify-process-fact enumerations + command-catalog-smoke trailing order for the two new commands.
